title: A first collaboration conversation with DEE-P Connections

sentences.text: We would welcome a connection between NSF families and DEE-P Connections (DEEP).
The atlas infers DEEP’s KCNQ2 connection from a partnership logo, not formal membership.
Published evidence suggests both disorders can involve an altered protein blocking the working protein; for NSF, this interpretation comes from a fruit-fly eye experiment.
Their symptom similarity is atlas-inferred, with confidence 0.48, below 0.5—not proof that research approaches will transfer.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: Citizen Health collects KCNQ2 medical-record histories; COMBINEDBrain manages a KCNQ2 biorepository.
Other possibilities include RARE-X, ENDD’s shared models, ESCO’s registry, STXBP1 Foundation grants and the Cambridge/Melbourne SYT1 collaboration.
These are starting points for enquiries, not verified NSF access.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: Please help confirm whether an NSF family group exists, whether a family network would help, and whether any registry accepts NSF.

Can we check primary microcephaly, profound intellectual disability and hydrops fetalis in KCNQ2; microcephaly, hydrops and tonic seizures in STXBP1; and burst-suppression EEG, microcephaly and profound disability in SNAP25?

Resource comparisons leave additional symptoms unnamed and list different mechanisms: excess or reduced protein activity for KCNQ2, excess activity or one insufficient working copy for STXBP1, and calcium-triggered nerve-message release for SYT1.
Please review those incomplete lists, SYT1’s EEG and microcephaly differences, eligibility, and necessary adaptations before reuse.
The KCNQ2 observational study names KCNQ2 specifically, and STXBP1’s proposed blocking mechanism is contested.
Send DEEP one email requesting a short conversation comparing notes on the proposed protein-blocking mechanism and possible family-network support.
Is there a dedicated NSF patient organisation?
Does any registry or natural history study enrol NSF families?
Is any interventional trial enrolling people with NSF-related disorders?
Does the atlas contain a documented animal or cell model with verified access?
Dear DEE-P Connections team,
I’m reaching out on behalf of NSF families.
Could we compare notes this month?
We would like to discuss the proposed shared protein-blocking mechanism.
Could you help us explore family connections and registry eligibility?
Thank you for considering this small first step.
[Your name], on behalf of families affected by NSF-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
